novel_features.name: Cross-product weekly diff
novel_features.description: Diff star ratings, new review counts, and badge changes across a list of products since a given window.
novel_features.rationale: Requires snapshotting products plus reviews in a local SQLite store and joining against a prior snapshot — no single G2 API call returns this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when a competitive-intel or PMM workflow asks for a head-to-head delta over a window. Replaces tab-by-tab eyeballing of multiple G2 pages.

novel_features.name: Credit-burn forecast
novel_features.description: Project month-end credit spend from trailing 14-day usage and refuse sync runs that would exceed remaining credits.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local mirror of credit_deductions; G2 surfaces a raw balance but no projection or budget guard.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this before a heavy sync to avoid mid-month throttling on credit-metered endpoints.

novel_features.name: Multi-product review FTS
novel_features.description: Full-text search across locally synced reviews, scoped by product list and structured filters (rating, segment).
novel_features.rationale: G2's site search is sentiment-shaped, not technical-fit-shaped; framework search over SQLite FTS5 inverts that.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when a buyer or competitive analyst wants to grep verbatims across many products' review corpora.

novel_features.name: Alternatives-signal switching threats
novel_features.description: Rank companies showing Alternatives-signal buyer intent against your product, weighted by visit count and employee size.
novel_features.rationale: G2's website paywalls this view; even the API doesn't return it ranked. Requires local SQLite query against buyer_intent_events.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when sales needs a ranked list of accounts evaluating switching away from your product.

novel_features.name: Category rising-challenger detector
novel_features.description: Per category, surface products in the top growth quartile by 30-day review velocity that aren't yet top quartile by absolute review count.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining products, categories, and reviews in local SQLite with a custom velocity metric.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when a PMM or competitive-intel analyst wants early signals on momentum players in a market.

novel_features.name: Buyer-intent triage CSV
novel_features.description: Filter buyer-intent rows by recency and minimum score and flatten nested firmographics into a sales-ready CSV.
novel_features.rationale: The raw API returns deeply nested JSON; the flat CSV projection with firmographics is what sales teams actually want.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this for a daily cron that pushes high-intent companies into the team's CRM or Slack.

novel_features.name: Reviews x competitors top-cons
novel_features.description: For each product in a list, return the lowest-rated reviews and their cons verbatims as JSON for downstream summarization.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-product aggregation in local SQLite; no single API call returns a competitor-by-competitor cons matrix.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when competitive intel needs to ground a complaint roundup across competitors; pipe the JSON to a summarizer of choice.

novel_features.name: Syndication-eligible review filter
novel_features.description: Filter synced reviews for the syndication-eligible flag, scoped by product and a recency window.
novel_features.rationale: G2's web UI buries this filter; surfacing it via a flag lets marketing sites auto-pull eligible reviews.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when wiring a marketing site or landing page to auto-refresh approved review quotes.

novel_features.name: Market-signal weekly diff
novel_features.description: Diff locally snapshotted market_signals for a category over a window; emit intent-score and visits-count deltas.
novel_features.rationale: Requires holding prior snapshots; the API returns a current state, not deltas.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this during a Friday competitive-intel report to spot category-level momentum changes.

narrative.headline: Every G2 Marketplace surface, plus a credit-aware local mirror, full-text review search, and buyer-intent triage no other G2 tool offers.
narrative.value_prop: g2-pp-cli unifies the v2 OpenAPI surface and the legacy syndication API behind one auth layer, mirrors products, reviews, vendors, categories, and buyer-intent into a local SQLite store, and adds workflows the Anthropic G2 MCP and every scraper miss: credit-burn forecasting (`credits forecast`), Alternatives-signal switching threats (`alt-track`), cross-product weekly diffs (`watch products`), and FTS over synced reviews.
narrative.auth_narrative: G2 ships two authentication surfaces. The v2 API uses OAuth 2.0 (`G2_CLIENT_ID` + `G2_CLIENT_SECRET`) plus an `AccountAPIToken` header (`G2_ACCOUNT_API_TOKEN`). The legacy syndication API (products, reviews, vendors, product_mappings, hashed_users) uses an `api_token` query parameter (`G2_SYNDICATION_TOKEN`). `g2-pp-cli auth login` walks you through both and stores them in `~/.config/g2-pp-cli/auth.json`. A paid G2 Sell-tier subscription is required for production endpoints; the developer portal at `my.g2.com/developers` provides a 1,000-call/month starter quota.

quickstart.comment: Validate auth, list granted OAuth scopes, and surface credit balance without burning a call.
Mirror products and categories into the local SQLite store.
Sync products then their reviews (hierarchical); FTS index updates automatically.
Daily buyer-intent triage flattened into a CSV ready for the CRM.
Project month-end credit spend before scheduling more sync runs.

troubleshoots.fix: Re-run `g2-pp-cli auth login` and confirm the OAuth scopes you registered include the resource you are calling (e.g., `buyer_intent.read`).
Syndication uses a separate `api_token` query parameter, not OAuth. Set `G2_SYNDICATION_TOKEN` or re-run `g2-pp-cli auth login --syndication`.

troubleshoots.symptom: 429 Too Many Requests / credit exhaustion mid-run
troubleshoots.fix: Check `g2-pp-cli credits balance --json` and forecast burn with `g2-pp-cli credits forecast --json`. Add `--budget-check` to future sync calls to abort early.
G2 intentionally hashes reviewer identities. The `hashed_users` payload exposes segment, industry, and country only. This is expected, not a bug.

troubleshoots.symptom: Sync returns 0 rows for products you can see on g2.com
troubleshoots.fix: Your developer-portal app must include `products.read` (and for reviews, `products.reviews.read`). Re-register at `my.g2.com/developers` with the full scope list.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for g2-pp-cli when a PMM, sales-ops, competitive-intel, or buyer-side workflow needs more than a chat-based MCP. The CLI keeps a local SQLite mirror of products, reviews, vendors, categories, and buyer-intent events so cron jobs, dashboards, and `claude`-piped agent workflows can run offline against a fresh corpus. Use it when credit-burn matters, when cross-product diffs are involved, or when full-text search over review bodies is the actual question.

recipes.title: Monday morning competitive snapshot
recipes.explanation: Joins yesterday's `products` snapshot with new `reviews` rows to produce a flat star-delta-by-competitor view; `--select` keeps the agent context short.

recipes.title: Daily buyer-intent triage to CSV
recipes.explanation: Cron-friendly: emits a flat CSV with company, domain, employees, industry, intent_score, page_type, signal_type.

recipes.title: Switching-threat list for sales
recipes.explanation: Surfaces companies showing Alternatives-signal intent against your product, ranked by visit count and employee size. The website paywalls this view.

recipes.title: Find rate-limit complaints across competitors
recipes.explanation: FTS5 query across all synced reviews; pair with `--select` to keep nested response payloads manageable for downstream agents.

recipes.title: Pre-sync credit check
recipes.explanation: Reads the local `credit_ledger`, projects month-end burn from the trailing 14-day average, and exits non-zero if a planned sync would exceed the remaining quota.
